observation: `agent-loop map build` with no `--paths` indexed 744 files in 3m29s and wrote a 100 MB `.agent-loop/map/php-symbols.json`, because it swept generated and gitignored PHP under `build/phpstan/cache/**` alongside real source. The same command also created `.agent-map/phpstan-cache/` at the project root: 16,526 files and 291 MB, outside `.agent-loop/` and outside anything the quick-start describes as workflow state. Re-running as `map build --paths=src,tests,bin` produced 74 files and a 4.5 MB index in 9.6s. Because `.agent-map/` is not gitignored and not in any scan-ignore list, it silently entered slop-scan's own scan scope: `composer run scan:self` went from roughly 3 seconds to not completing within 300 seconds, and the file count in scope went from about 180 to 16,668.

evidence.summary: Wrote 744 file(s), 209212 relation(s) in 3m28.944s; `du -sh .agent-loop/map/` reported 97M and `du -sh .agent-map` reported 291M across 16,526 files, all under `.agent-map/phpstan-cache/cache/PHPStan/`.
Wrote 74 file(s), 6416 relation(s) in 9.587s into a 4.5 MB index: same useful content, 22x faster, 22x smaller.

`find . -path ./vendor -prune -o -path ./build -prune -o \( -name "*.php" -o -name "*.md" \) -print | cut -d/ -f2 | sort | uniq -c` attributed 16,486 of 16,668 in-scope files to `.agent-map`. After `rm -rf .agent-map` and adding the tooling directories to the repository scan ignores, `scan . --json` completed in 3.594s.

hypothesis: The default path set is "the repository", which is correct for a small hand-written tree and wrong for any repository that keeps generated PHP on disk. The PHPStan cache location looks like an implementation detail of agent-map that predates the "all workflow state lives below .agent-loop/" consolidation and was never moved with the rest.
validated_conclusion: A tool that writes hundreds of megabytes into a project root has to say so in the layout it publishes, and `.agent-map/phpstan-cache/` contradicts the documented promise that workflow state lives below `.agent-loop/`. Defaults that scan "everything" should respect `.gitignore`, or default to the project's Composer autoload roots, because generated PHP is indistinguishable from source to a naive walker. The damage here was not the disk: it was that another tool in the same repository silently changed behavior because of files it never agreed to see.
